maidstone.s1_head: Charity and volunteer kit across Maidstone
s1loc: Maidstone's emergency food runs through the Maidstone Family Food Bank and the borough's network of community pantries and food hubs, while FareShare Kent moves surplus food from the trade out to local groups. Heart of Kent Hospice cares for people across mid-Kent and raises money through around fourteen charity shops from Maidstone out to West Malling, Staplehurst and Headcorn, and Involve Kent helps match volunteers to projects. The big food-redistribution and foodbank networks and dozens of tiny volunteer-run groups all draw helpers from across the county town.

The sector here runs at every size. National and regional charities keep shops and central buying alongside hospice and air-ambulance fundraising, while small community groups, foodbanks, pantries and volunteer-run projects work on a shoestring across Tovil, Shepway and Park Wood. We are set up to serve the national charity with shops on the high street and the one-room foodbank alike, with trade accounts for the big buyers and direct online ordering, no minimum, for the smallest group.
